scope: Manager 4.17.x systemic product defects and material process escapes

defects.title: Registration cleanup deletes committed per-instance state after activation failure
defects.preconditions: Register an existing Hub, commit its registry row, then fail during optional activation/switch.
defects.bad_behavior: Catch cleanup can remove newly-created instance state after the registry row is already durable, leaving committed registry state that references missing instance state.
defects.root_cause: Transaction cleanup did not distinguish definite pre-commit failure from durable commit followed by post-commit failure.

defects.title: Frontend accepts non-canonical instance ID before state-relative path construction
defects.preconditions: Corrupt active/registry metadata supplies a matching non-empty instance ID that is not a canonical GUID.
defects.bad_behavior: Frontend can embed the unvalidated ID into state/instances and exchange/instances paths.
defects.root_cause: Metadata agreement was treated as identity validity; canonical GUID validation happened too late or not at all.

defects.title: Registered Genesis cancellation is treated as successful staging
defects.preconditions: Interactive nested Genesis returns its clean-cancel outcome without producing Hub/CURRENT materialization.
defects.bad_behavior: Registered Genesis continues into validation as if staging succeeded and attempts to validate artifacts that were never created.
defects.root_cause: Nested action result did not distinguish cancellation from successful materialization.

defects.title: ChatGPT exchange can combine destination for instance A with CURRENT from instance B
defects.preconditions: Frontend captures exchange destination while A is active, another process switches active instance, then CURRENT is resolved again.
defects.bad_behavior: B's CURRENT can be copied into A's exchange tree.
defects.root_cause: Source and destination were not derived from one immutable captured instance context.

defects.title: Registered Genesis directory publication can change meaning if destination appears
defects.preconditions: Genesis validates a free destination, then another actor creates it before PowerShell Move-Item publishes the staged Hub.
defects.bad_behavior: Move-Item can nest the staged Hub inside the now-occupied destination while the registry records the parent path.
defects.root_cause: Container-aware Move-Item semantics were used instead of fail-if-destination-exists publication.

defects.title: Existing-Hub state publication retains destination-sensitive Move-Item semantics
defects.preconditions: New-RegisteredInstanceStateFromVault validates staging, then instance state root appears before publication.
defects.bad_behavior: The staging directory can be moved inside an occupied destination and registration can proceed without a fresh exact baseline check at commit boundary.
defects.root_cause: The same destination-sensitive publication primitive fixed for Genesis remained in the registration/bootstrap path.

defects.title: Candidate transport documented ingress points at global inbox after registry activation
defects.preconditions: Multi-Hub registry is active and user follows the documented/OpenInbox candidate-transport ingress path.
defects.bad_behavior: Input can be placed in global state/inbox while runtime consumes the active instance inbox, making the documented candidate invisible.
defects.root_cause: User-facing ingress and runtime discovery changed ownership at different layers.

defects.title: Registered Genesis rejects equivalent Windows path casing
defects.preconditions: Canonical hubs root and requested path parent are semantically equal Windows paths with different casing.
defects.bad_behavior: Case-sensitive comparison rejects a valid target.
defects.root_cause: Ordinal/case-sensitive path equality was used for Windows filesystem identity.

defects.title: Frontend Hub package import can target A while runtime update resolves B
defects.preconditions: Frontend captures A's inbox, copies a package, another process switches active instance, then a new Manager process starts UpdateHub.
defects.bad_behavior: Package remains under A while runtime resolves B, causing stranded input or wrong-instance operation.
defects.root_cause: Frontend-to-runtime handoff did not carry immutable captured instance context.

defects.title: Development validation path filters miss inherited regression-only changes
defects.preconditions: Only an inherited 4.17.2/4.17.3 regression script changes.
defects.bad_behavior: Development validation can fail to trigger even though its top-level regression chain executes that script transitively.
defects.root_cause: Workflow path filters were narrower than the transitive executable dependency graph.

defects.title: Expected single-instance context is not freshly revalidated after lock acquisition
defects.preconditions: ExpectedSingleInstance UpdateHub starts before registry exists and waits for Manager lock while another process initializes the registry.
defects.bad_behavior: Cached registry-active=false allows the operation to continue after lock without detecting the new registry.
defects.root_cause: Transaction-boundary validation trusted invocation-time cached registry state instead of re-reading durable state.

defects.title: Active Hub inbox scan is incorrectly gated by global Manager inbox existence
defects.preconditions: Registry active; active per-instance Hub inbox exists; global Manager inbox is absent.
defects.bad_behavior: Quick status/UI can report no Hub packages because instance-owned scans are nested under a global inbox existence condition.
defects.root_cause: Instance-owned discovery retained an unrelated global-state precondition after ownership split.

defects.title: Old Manager UpdateAll restart cannot preserve newly introduced Hub context token
defects.preconditions: Supported 4.17.5 -> 4.17.6 UpdateAll transition crosses process restart while active Hub can change.
defects.bad_behavior: Old Manager restarts new Manager with tokenless -UpdateAll, so the new process can resolve a different Hub.
defects.root_cause: Safety token existed only in the new executable contract; the old executable could not carry it across the compatibility restart boundary.

defects.title: InitializeInstanceRegistry reports success for an existing invalid registry
defects.preconditions: instances.json exists but registry or active selection cannot resolve safely; startup allows InitializeInstanceRegistry to enter recovery path.
defects.bad_behavior: Initialization can return success based on file existence while multi-Hub remains unusable.
defects.root_cause: Existence was treated as successful initialization rather than resolving and validating the authoritative registry plus active selection.

defects.title: Documented UPDATE_ALL compatibility alias bypasses context-capturing frontend
defects.preconditions: Multi-Hub registry active and user invokes supported UPDATE_ALL.cmd alias.
defects.bad_behavior: Alias directly invokes tokenless runtime UpdateAll and is rejected by the safety guard, even though canonical frontend captures context correctly.
defects.root_cause: Compatibility command generation did not share the canonical frontend orchestration contract.

defects.title: Existing-Hub registration can commit a CURRENT that can never activate
defects.preconditions: Hub/CURRENT are structurally coherent but CURRENT artifact status is CANDIDATE/non-approved.
defects.bad_behavior: Registration can durably add a registry row that later fails every activation/switch attempt.
defects.root_cause: Final commit validation checked content/identity coherence but not the stronger activation-eligibility contract.

defects.title: Recovery switch and bind are blocked by broken active Hub resolution
defects.preconditions: Registry exists and current active Hub is missing/corrupt while another healthy registered/rebind target is available.
defects.bad_behavior: Early Resolve-RegisteredInstanceContextEarly throws before dispatch and recovery allowlist omits SwitchInstanceId/BindInstancePath, so normal recovery cannot reach its handler.
defects.root_cause: Command dispatch requires successful validation of the broken active state before determining that the requested command is a recovery operation.

defects.title: Registry activation silently strands pending global Hub inputs
defects.preconditions: Single-instance global Manager inbox contains Hub APPROVED, CANDIDATE or candidate-transport inputs when InitializeInstanceRegistry activates per-instance state.
defects.bad_behavior: Bootstrap creates an empty instance-owned inbox and changes Hub discovery to it without migration, rejection or fail-closed precondition, leaving old valid inputs invisible to normal workflows.
defects.root_cause: The ownership transition commits before accounting for already-reachable pending state whose discovery root changes at activation.
